docs.pageTitle: Docs: test a keyboard layout without learning it · Kawalyser
docs.description: How Kawalyser works: ready-made layouts, Kalamine import, 1DK, Repeat and Magic keys, Clever Keys, your own corpus, and every statistic explained.

hero.title: Test a keyboard layout before you learn it
hero.intro: Kawalyser types a long text on a keyboard layout and counts how your fingers move. In a few seconds, you know whether a layout is comfortable, without spending weeks learning it.

purpose.title: Why Kawalyser
purpose.intro: A keyboard layout is the choice of which character goes on which key. QWERTY is one, but many others aim to type more comfortably. Kawalyser helps you choose and tune them.

items.answer: Kawalyser measures it first, on real text, before you commit.

items.problem: Modern layouts rely on tricks most analyzers ignore: a dead key for accents, Repeat and Magic keys, Clever Keys.
items.answer: Kawalyser types the text the way your keyboard would, tricks included.

items.problem: The analyzer these layouts come from is an Excel workbook: slow, and not interactive.
items.answer: Kawalyser keeps its algorithms and its results in a fast, free website. Move a key, analyze again.

presets.title: Pick a layout
presets.text: Propergol, Ergo-L, Erglace, Strud-L or StrudE-L, with their thumb keys and replacements, in one click.

toml.title: Import your layout
toml.text: Load any Kalamine .toml file. The characters land on the right keys by themselves.

edit.title: Move keys
edit.text: Drag a character onto another key, or select a zone and type. Undo and redo at will.

replacements.title: Add replacements
replacements.text: Import a .json file of Magic rules and Clever Keys, and choose how many apply.

corpus.title: Use your own text
corpus.text: Import a .txt corpus in any language. It never leaves your browser.

analyze.title: Analyze
analyze.text: Finger load, rolls, same-finger bigrams, scissors and more, on a French or English corpus, or yours.

download.title: Download the details
download.text: Export every n-gram and every difficulty as CSV files for your spreadsheet.

shapes.title: Choose the keyboard
shapes.text: Split keyboards with 40 or 34 keys, thumb keys included.

steps.title: Choose a layout
steps.text: Pick one in the Layout list, or import your .toml file.

steps.title: Adjust it
steps.text: Move characters, add replacements, pick a corpus.

steps.title: Run the analysis
steps.text: Click Run analysis. It takes a few seconds.

steps.title: Read the results
steps.text: Compare the statistics, then download the details to dig deeper.

keys.title: Special keys
keys.intro: Kawalyser understands the keys that make modern layouts efficient. On the map, each one is written with a symbol.

dead.name: 1DK dead key
dead.text: One dead key opens a second layer: press it, then a key, to type the character drawn at the bottom right of that key.

repeat.name: Repeat
repeat.text: Types the previous key press again, so a doubled letter needs no move of the same finger.

magic.name: Magic
magic.text: Its output depends on the previous key press. Your replacements file says what it types.
magic.example: u then # types ui on Propergol

clever.name: Clever Keys
clever.text: Firmware rules that type a whole string from a short sequence, sometimes only at the start or end of a word.
clever.example: q then n types quand on Propergol

keys.levelsIntro: The Replacements list sets which rules of your file the analysis applies.

levels.raw: The text as it is. Repeat still serves if it is on the map.
levels.corrections: Adds the essential corrections, and the dead key strings of several characters.
levels.clever: Adds the optional corrections too: the Clever Keys.

metrics.title: The statistics
metrics.intro: Kawalyser cleans the corpus, types it on your layout, then cuts it into bigrams (two key presses) and trigrams (three). The text is read in lowercase: Shift is left out. For every difficulty, lower is better.
metrics.bigramsIntro: Two key presses in a row with the same hand. Each diagram shows a left hand: 1 is the first press, 2 the second.

sfb.name: SFB · Same finger bigram
sfb.text: Two different keys with the same finger: the slowest move to type.

skb.name: SKB · Same key bigram
skb.text: The same key twice, as in a doubled letter. Repeat avoids it.

lsb.name: LSB · Lateral stretch bigram
lsb.text: Neighboring fingers two columns apart: the hand stretches sideways.

fsb.name: FSB · Full scissor bigram
fsb.text: Two rows apart, a long finger below a shorter one: the fingers fold the wrong way.

hsb.name: HSB · Half scissor bigram
hsb.text: The same fold, one row apart.

rjb.name: RJB · Row jump bigram
rjb.text: Two rows apart, without a scissor.

load.name: Finger and hand load
load.text: The share of key presses on each finger and each hand, home row keys apart.

alternation.name: Alternation
alternation.text: Three presses: one hand, the other, then the first again.

rolls.name: Rolls
rolls.text: Two presses with one hand, one with the other, inward (towards the thumb) or outward.

oneHand.name: One-hand trigrams
oneHand.text: Three presses with one hand, in one direction.

redirects.name: Redirects
redirects.text: Three presses with one hand that change direction. Bad when none is on the index or the thumb.

sfs.name: SFS and STS · Same finger skipgrams
sfs.text: The first and third presses of a trigram on the same finger. SFS leaves out the trigrams with a space, STS counts them.

fss.name: FSS · Full scissor skipgram
fss.text: A full scissor between the first and third presses of a trigram.

cc.name: CC · Cognitive load
cc.text: How often a replacement rule applies, per key press of the original text.

shs.name: SHS · Same hand sequences
shs.text: Runs of four or more presses with one hand inside a word. Long runs that come back score more.

missing.name: Not on the map
missing.text: The most frequent characters of the corpus that no key types.

toml.title: Layout: Kalamine .toml
toml.text: The format of {kalamine}, the layout creation tool. Kawalyser reads the base layer, and the dead key layer drawn on the right of each key.
points: The number row and AltGr are left out.
The bottom left key goes to the left thumb, Magic, Repeat and space to the other thumbs.
A character on two keys of the main block stops the import: Kawalyser could not tell which one you type.

replacements.title: Replacements: .json
replacements.text: Each rule reads: to write text, type keys. In keys, * is the dead key, $ Repeat and # Magic. Essential corrections apply from the Essential level, optional ones at the Essential + Optional level.

corpus.title: Corpus: .txt
corpus.text: Any plain text, in any language, up to 10 MB.
points: UTF-8 is best. A file in another encoding is read as Windows-1252, with a warning.
Curly apostrophes become straight ones, and ... becomes … when the map has it.
Characters missing from the map are left out of the statistics, and listed under the results.

privacy.title: Your data
items: No account, no sign-up, no ads.
The site's French and English corpora stay on the server: they are never sent to your browser.
Your own corpus stays in your browser: it is analyzed there and never sent to the server.
To analyze the French or English corpus, your layout and replacements go to the server for the time of the analysis.
Your layout, replacements and corpus are kept in your browser, so that you find them on your next visit.

items.question: Why does a character of my text not count?
items.answer: The analysis reads the text in lowercase and leaves Shift out. A character that no key types without Shift, directly or after the dead key, is left out of the statistics. The Not on the map card lists the most frequent ones.

items.question: Can I test a second dead key or a second Magic key?
items.answer: Yes. Place a rare character, such as ¤, on a key, then use it in the keys of your replacements file. The rule ion → i¤ turns it into a second Magic key. Pick a character your corpus does not contain.

items.question: Why do my numbers differ from the Excel workbook?
items.answer: The site corrects a few behaviors of the workbook, decided with its author. The {readme} lists them.

items.question: My keyboard is not split.
items.answer: For now, Kawalyser only knows split keyboards with 40 or 34 keys.

source.title: Source code and credits
